conflicts: Price: the Handi Quilter product page now shows a range starting at $5,495 and Amazon (B08P3SRX98, Moxie with 8 ft Loft frame) shows $5,495, while our earlier spec recorded $5,995 regular price at Village Sewing on 2026-09-29; the maker's base configuration behind $5,495 is not labelled, so the $5,495 figure is a seen price, not a confirmed bundle.

Needle sizes: the maker manual gives 80/12 to 130/21, while our earlier spec from a Handi Quilter support article said sizes 12 to 20; the manual figure is used and the support article was not re-fetched.

Included feet: the Handi Quilter product page lists a ruler foot and open-toe foot in one bullet and a closed-toe foot and open-toe foot in another, so the second included foot is unconfirmed; our earlier '20 needles included' came from a dealer and no maker document read supports it, so it is removed.
Frame height: our earlier spec attached 33 to 44 in to the frame generally, while the maker states that range for the Little Foot frame only and gives no range for the Loft frame.
Weight: the maker page gives 58 lb packaging weight, which is shipping weight, and an Amazon seller listing shows 50 lb item weight; no maker machine weight was found, so weight stays [verify].

Warranty: the 2020 maker manual says the 5 year electrical warranty is void if the machine is left plugged in when not in use, while the maker warranty page does not say so; both are listed and the warranty page is not Moxie-specific.

Throat: the maker says '15-inch throat space' and the manual gives a sewing opening of 8.25 x 15.00 in without labelling which figure is height, and neither says needle to body; the maker's own figure for safe usable quilting area on a frame is about 10 in.
Speed: 1,800 spm maximum (maker page and manual) against a 50 to 800 spm cruise range; the manual also gives 25 and 50 spm as the manual-mode floor in different places.

Manual source: the maker manual was read from a dealer-hosted copy (sewingmachinesplus.com, version 1.0, 10/2020) because handiquilter.com downloads returned a bot challenge, so it may not match the current maker file.

ownerThemes.theme: After a year an owner still calls it a brilliant small machine but notes tension changes take a moment to settle and that moving the head after stitching can snap the top thread and force a rethread.

Tension, thread breaking and fabric bunching are the recurring troubleshooting topics; the fix path is bobbin winding and threading checks first, and retiming by a Handi Quilter retailer if shredding persists.
Handi Quilter's own support pages treat tension and thread shredding as expected setup problems with a defined checklist, which suggests they are common enough to document.

editorial.verdict: A 15 in head on a frame: Handi Quilter lists regulated stitching and an 8 ft Loft frame, but gives about 10 in of usable quilting area and tension reports recur.
editorial.whoFor: A home quilter with room for an 8 ft frame who wants an entry long-arm on a frame with built-in stitch regulation and is not quilting for clients.
editorial.skipIf: You want wide custom work (the maker puts usable area at about 10 in), have no room for a frame, or only quilt lap size and smaller on a sit-down machine.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Handi Quilter Moxie and the Moxie XL?
faqs.a: From Handi Quilter's product pages, the Moxie XL lists 18 in of throat space and 2,100 stitches per minute, against 15 in and 1,800 on the Moxie. The XL also lists a 4.3 in display and a 72 lb packaging weight, against a 1.44 in display and 58 lb on the Moxie. Packaging weight is shipping weight, not machine weight. These are maker figures; we have not collected an owner read for the XL.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Handi Quilter Moxie?
faqs.a: Owners who are happy with it point to the built-in stitch regulator, and some report tension they like once the machine is set up. Complaints cluster around the frame (sagging, hard to move smoothly), a clunky sound, numb hands after long sessions and no automatic threading or thread cutting. The read covers 20 Reddit threads and 2 retailer pages from 2021 to 2026, a small sample, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented. Amazon shows 4.8 from 17 ratings, which is seller-collected and pools a second ASIN; the Sewing Machines Plus page (4.55 from 29) is not counted here because none of its sampled reviews name the Moxie.

faqs.q: How much does the Handi Quilter Moxie cost?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter's product page shows a range of $5,495 to $12,690, depending on the frame and Pro-Stitcher options (seen 2026-10-02). Amazon listed the Moxie with an 8 ft Loft frame at $5,495 on the same date, and an earlier dealer figure was $5,995 at Village Sewing (seen 2026-09-29). The maker does not label the base configuration behind $5,495, so confirm what is included [verify].

faqs.q: Does the Handi Quilter Moxie come with a frame?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter says the Moxie includes the 8 ft HQ Loft Frame, which upgrades to 10 ft with a 2 ft extension kit, and that it is also compatible with the 5 ft Little Foot Frame. The maker page frame selector changes the price, and the base configuration behind the $5,495 starting price is not labelled. Ask the retailer which frame the quoted price includes [verify].

faqs.q: Is stitch regulation built into the Handi Quilter Moxie?
faqs.a: Yes, per Handi Quilter. The page and manual list Precision and Cruise regulation plus a Manual mode, selected on the display, at 4 to 18 stitches per inch in regulated mode. Owners who mention it like it: one advises prioritising it above other extras and another says it goes down to 4 stitches per inch for basting. The maker does not show how well regulation tracks, so that part is not verified.

faqs.q: Can you add Pro-Stitcher to the Handi Quilter Moxie?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter lists the Moxie as Pro-Stitcher Lite compatible, and says all new Handi Quilter movable machines are Pro-Stitcher ready with cabling pre-installed. Pro-Stitcher is an option on the maker's configurator. Its price was not published on the pages we read [verify].

faqs.q: What needles does the Handi Quilter Moxie take?
faqs.a: The maker manual lists needle system 134 in sizes 80/12 to 130/21. An earlier spec from a Handi Quilter support article said sizes 12 to 20, so we use the manual figure. The manual was read from a dealer-hosted 2020 copy, so confirm against the current file [verify].

faqs.q: Does the Handi Quilter Moxie use M class or L class bobbins?
faqs.a: M class. Handi Quilter lists a high-speed rotary hook with a large-capacity M class bobbin, and the manual specifies an aluminum M class bobbin with a type MF bobbin case.

faqs.q: What warranty does the Handi Quilter Moxie have?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter's warranty page lists 90 days parts and labor, 10 years on casting or machining defects in the sewing head, and 5 years each on mechanical and electrical parts, with the customer paying labor and shipping after the first 90 days. The text covers the 'HQ Quilting Machine', not the Moxie by name. The 2020 manual also says the electrical warranty is void if the machine is left plugged in when not in use; the warranty page does not say so [verify].
